lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: Feedback Friends
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 5, Session 1
lesson.footer: Persuasive Writing | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 5 Session 1

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY11 re-reading and editing their own texts and the texts of others using agreed criteria; VC2E5LY01 interaction skills, questioning to clarify meaning
plan.shape: model, sort, conference: the teacher gives feedback on a weak sample, students sort helpful from unhelpful comments, then run a peer conference with the checklist and plan their own revisions
plan.criticalFeature: useful feedback points at one sentence and says one thing to try
decisionPoints: the choice check: the best grow comment
the exit board: a grow comment for a new paragraph
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. The checklist asks: did the writer do all three, for their reader?
plan.catchUp: No finished draft? Pair them with a partner to give feedback first, then conference with the teacher about their own plan.

studentTools: Each student's complete draft from Week 4
Sticky notes in two colours (glow and grow)
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: Glow (a sentence that works and why) / Grow (one thing to try) / Question (something you wondered)

resources.label: Big Piece Checklist
resources.description: The agreed criteria for the big piece, used by partners today and by the writer when revising and editing all week.
resources.title: Big Piece Checklist
resources.subtitle: Tick what you find. Then write one glow, one grow and one question.

checklist: Each body paragraph starts with its claim
Proof with who said it, then This means...
Answer back: Some people say... However...
Conclusion: restate, sum up, call to action
Powerful words that are still true
Two or more devices, and linking words between paragraphs

blocks.text: Writer: my revision plan (three changes I will make)

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: this week we polish and publish, starting with feedback from a friend.

slides.title: For the teacher: Week 5 at a glance
lines: This week: feedback, revise, edit, publish. Every student has a complete draft from Week 4.
Today: peer feedback with the Big Piece Checklist (agreed criteria, VC2E5LY11).
Session 3 includes the crossword fun activity (persuasion words) for early finishers and the warm-up.
Session 4: publish and share with the audience you chose (another class, newsletter, a real organisation).
Unit anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it.
slides.notes: Teacher-facing only. Confirm the publishing audience before Session 4.

Print one Big Piece Checklist per student for the conference (reused all week), then the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Pair a confident writer with a developing one.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to give and use feedback that makes writing stronger.
successCriteria: I can check a draft against our checklist.
I can give feedback that points to a sentence and suggests one thing to try.
I can choose which feedback to use and plan my changes.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Every published writer has an editor. Today you are each other's.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Checking against the checklist is where we start.
Feedback that points and suggests is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 checking against criteria is reachable for all; SC2 specific feedback is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 choosing and planning revisions is the stretch.

slides.title: Which comment would help you?
lines: Your question at the start pulled me in. Try adding a fact after your second sentence.

notes.answer: the second - it points at a sentence and says what to try
beats: SAY: Two people read your draft. Here's what they say.
Which would actually help you improve it?
ASK: Which comment helps you more? First or second?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, 1 or 2... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What does the second one do that the first doesn't?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: it says which part; it says what to try
SAY: Today you'll be the second kind of reader for a friend.
trap: preferring It's good because it feels nicer.
Fix: ask what would you change after It's good? Student sees nothing.

slides.meaning: Information that helps someone improve their work.
slides.example: Your hook pulled me in. Try a fact after it.

notes.answer: information that helps someone improve their work
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Feedback. Say it with me. Feedback.
SAY: Feedback is information that helps you improve.
A glow says what works. A grow says what to try.
ASK: In the example, which part is the glow and which is the grow?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: glow is the hook; grow is the fact
trap: thinking feedback means saying what's wrong.
Fix: say every feedback slip starts with a glow.
notes.prep: Glow and grow are the class protocol all week.

slides.title: Watch me give feedback
slides.extract: Zoos are bad for polar bears. They are really, really bad. Polar bears like the cold. Zoos are hot. I think zoos should maybe not have them. That is why.
highlights: Polar bears like the cold. Zoos are hot.
I think zoos should maybe not have them.
slides.source: Sample draft, written for this session

notes.answer: glow: the cold and hot contrast; grow: high modality and proof; question: which zoos?
beats: READ the sample aloud once. Use the checklist beside it.
SAY: First, a glow. I point at a sentence that works.
POINT to Polar bears like the cold. Zoos are hot.
SAY: Glow: those two short sentences make the problem clear. Nice contrast.
POINT to maybe.
SAY: Grow: swap I think... maybe for must, then add proof with who said it.
ASK: What question would you ask this writer?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: which zoos? how hot? who says bears suffer?
trap: a grow with three things to fix at once.
Fix: student picks the one change that would help most.
notes.stretch: Rank three grows by which helps the reader most.
notes.help: Use the checklist: find the first unticked box.
notes.prep: The model. Critical feature: useful feedback points at one sentence and says one thing to try. The sample is deliberately weak.

slides.title: Helpful or not?
slides.pivot: ask: could the writer act on it tomorrow?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: how would you fix the unhelpful one?

items.text: Your question in line 1 really pulled me in.
items.answer: 1 - helpful glow: it points at a sentence

items.text: In paragraph 2, add who said your fact, like According to NASA.
items.answer: 1 - helpful grow: one clear thing to try
2 - not helpful: about the topic, not the writing

items.expect: 2 fingers. ACCEPT: 1 if they say which
items.say: Not yet. Which words? Point to them. Tick or fix.

say: One finger helpful, two not helpful.
Helpful means the writer knows what to do next.
trap: voting Good job helpful because it's kind.
Fix: ask what would the writer change? Student re-votes.
notes.stretch: Rewrite each unhelpful comment to be helpful.
notes.help: Ask: does it point at a sentence?
notes.prep: Guided sort of feedback quality. SC2.

slides.title: Which is the best grow comment?
slides.prompt: The paragraph has a strong claim but no evidence.

options.misconception: vague; the writer doesn't know what to do

options.text: Add a fact after your topic sentence, and say who said it.

options.misconception: judges the opinion, not the writing

notes.answer: B - it points to where and says what to add
beats: SAY: The paragraph needs proof. Which comment would get it there?
ASK: Which is the best grow comment?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: turn A into a helpful grow.
Less -> run the could-they-act-on-it test, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. It says where, what and how. The writer can do it straight away.
trap: pointing to C because honest feedback is good.
Fix: say we judge the writing, not the opinion.
notes.prep: Decision point before the conference. Under 80% means one pair models the conference for the class first.

slides.title: Turn it into a grow
slides.pivot: ask: which sentence, and what exactly should they try?
slides.followUp: cold call one board: could the writer do that tomorrow?

items.answer: In paragraph 1, add a fact that proves your claim, and who said it.
End with a call to action: tell the principal exactly what to do.
In line 3, swap bad for a powerful true word like harmful.

say: These comments mean well, but they don't help yet.
Rewrite each one as a grow the writer can act on.
trap: rewriting it longer but still vague: Add more good stuff please.
Fix: student names the sentence and the exact change.
notes.stretch: Add the reason: because your reader needs...
notes.prep: Guided rewriting of vague feedback. SC2.

slides.title: Feedback conference
slides.task: Swap drafts and give feedback on the Checklist. Then work through your Worksheet and plan your changes.
slides.frame: Glow: ___ works because ___. Grow: try ___ in ___.

notes.answer: feedback that points at a sentence; a three-point revision plan
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Be the reader your partner needs. Kind, specific, helpful.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Read grow notes: does each one point at a sentence?
ASK: Is your feedback written and handed back?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up at 15 minutes
TIME 22 minutes: 15 reading and writing feedback, 7 planning.
trap: only glows, because they don't want to upset a friend.
Fix: say a grow is a gift: it makes their writing win.
notes.stretch: Extension: rank feedback, then give a second full conference.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: glow-or-grow choices, a first fix done, a revision frame.
notes.prep: Independent application. The revision plan drives Session 2. SC2 and SC3.

slides.extendedTask: a peer feedback conference, then a worksheet ending in a three-change revision plan

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Kids should have more PE. It's fun. Everyone likes it. PE is good.
Write one helpful grow comment for this writer.

notes.answer: e.g. After line 1, add a fact about exercise and who said it
beats: SAY: A new paragraph from a new writer. Help them.
ASK: Write one helpful grow comment.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: points at a sentence or word, says one thing to try
RECORD who writes a vague grow. Revision small group tomorrow.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new paragraph. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Which piece of feedback will you use first? Tell your partner why.

notes.answer: open - listen for a specific change linked to the reader
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How useful was the feedback you gave?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: Which feedback will you use first, and why?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: adding my source, because it makes my claim believable
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit boards. Keep the checklists in the books. SC2.
